summary: Lane County station on Saddle Mountain: a ranger cabin burned in 1912, lookouts were posted in the 1920s and 1930s, and a 1937 pole tower is now gone.

facts.status_note: The register says the 1937 pole tower is now gone; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Forest rangers' cabin on Saddle Mountain destroyed by fire, June 1912
Two men building a replacement ranger cabin, reported in July 1913
Lookouts stationed on the mountain during the summer; Mr. and Mrs. Wm. Louney named
Lynch named as patrolman (R. E. Lynch in the 1928 item, Robert Lynch in the 1929 item)
Cecil Thompson stationed at the lookout; paid $85 per month
Panorama of the lookout captioned 4-18-34 on the register; the Forest Lookouts page lists panorama photos under April 12, 1934
Pole L-4 tower built on the site; the register says it is now gone
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, November 15, 2010

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register caption reads 4-18-34; the Forest Lookouts page lists panorama photos under April 12, 1934. The sources do not say whether they are the same photographs, so the story reports both.

sources.title: Saddle Mountain Guard Station - Forest Lookouts

notes_for_editor: Two sources that agree on place, agency and county. The newspaper items on the Forest Lookouts page are quoted without full citations, and they mix the cabin, the station and the lookout; the story keeps the 1912 and 1913 cabin separate from the lookout posts. The register's 1937 pole tower is the only built date for a tower. The brief's coordinates (44.1859, -123.9574) sit about 0.8 km from the register point (44.18519, -123.96729); no source says which is the exact site. Another Saddle Mountain lookout (us-or-saddle-mountain) is a different site and should not be merged.
